messages:
maria.g: Heads-up — during the int4 preflight for v2.1-quant we saw a small but consistent degradation on the 'long-doc recall' slice (docs > 4k tokens).
chris: saw that in the dashboard too. delta ~ -0.035 MRR on that slice across the 2h smoke. overall metrics look fine.
priya: is that delta with the same prompt set vs baseline v2.0-fp16?
maria.g: yes, baseline is v2.0-fp16 pinned. numbers: baseline MRR 0.412 -> quant MRR 0.398. sample size ~ 3200 across the slice.
samir: 3.5% is notable. what are our current auto-fallback rules for long-doc slices?
priya: I think our preflight rule is: if any critical slice has delta <= -0.03 AND p-value < 0.05 => fail and autofallback. but we also gate on absolute sample count > 500.
maria.g: sample count is >500 so rule would trigger. want to double-check p-value calc — I saw the eval-bot flagged it as borderline.
eval-bot: Automated eval report: slice=long-docs(>4k); n=3214; delta=-0.0349; p=0.047; CI=[-0.060,-0.009]; drift=low; notes=slightly elevated variance on suffix prompts. Link: https://console.redwood/testing/runs/2026-01-17/1709999000
chris: p=0.047, so technically below 0.05 — autofallback would fire. but do we want to rely on a single metric?
priya: we usually require at least 2 failures across orthogonal metrics (MRR + exact-match or BLEU-like) before full autofallback for long-doc slices. the preflight microconfig might be using only MRR here.
maria.g: hmm config snippet from the rollout gate:
```
"safety_checks": [
  {"slice": "long-docs", "metric": "mrr", "threshold": -0.03, "pvalue": 0.05},
]
"hard_autofallback": true
```
priya: that explains it — current gate is being aggressive. suggestion: change to composite rule: require delta<-0.03 AND secondary metric delta<-0.02 OR p<0.01 for single-metric triggers.
samir: or add a fudge window for low-variance slices: if CI width > 0.04 then require larger delta. here CI width is 0.051, so variance relatively high.
maria.g: good point. I worry about masking real regressions though. maybe we add a short-lived hold (quiet-burn) instead of immediate autofallback for fractional traffic. e.g., block autofallback automatic for preflight but mark run as FAIL and require a manual ack to promote.
chris: conservative approach ok for this case — preflight should be cautious. but our whole point of autofallback is to avoid promotions that break prod. how often do these borderline p-value triggers produce false positives?
priya: historically ~12% of preflight p<0.05 triggers end up being not reproducible on a subsequent 6h run (we keep a log). Most are variance/noise.
eval-bot: Historical autocheck summary: p<0.05 single-metric triggers (n=127) => reproducible-regression in 111 runs (87%), non-reproducible in 16 runs (13%).
maria.g: ok. proposal: update the gate for long-docs to: require (delta_mrr < -0.03 && p < 0.01) OR (delta_mrr < -0.05 && p < 0.05) OR (delta_mrr < -0.03 && delta_exact < -0.02). keep hard_autofallback=false for preflight, but set alert and block automatic promote.
samir: LGTM. can you add a brief doc note and a one-line migration for cfg?
maria.g: will do. I'll open PR to rollout-config with the patch and link the preflight run.
chris: quick action item: add long-doc sample stratification so repeats of same doc don't inflate n. we saw a few duplicates in the sample.
priya: noted — will add de-dup and bump min_unique_docs to 400 for the slice.
maria.g: thanks — I'll follow up after PR. :thumbsup:
chris: :eyes:
priya: tagging release lead @samir to ack the plan?
samir: ack. sounding reasonable. once PR lands, re-run preflight for the same seed and let's see if the signal persists.
maria.g: thanks all — filing the PR now and scheduling a replay for tomorrow morning.
